what: Insulet makes the Omnipod: a small insulin pump that sticks to the skin with no tubing, replaced every three days, used by people with type 1 and increasingly type 2 diabetes.
customers: People with diabetes and their endocrinologists, paid for by insurers and pharmacy benefit plans.
money: pods and controllers sold through pharmacies
the same products in Europe and other markets
pumps made for other pharmaceutical companies
moat: Selling through the pharmacy benefit rather than medical equipment channels, which makes starting on Omnipod far easier than on a tubed pump, and a disposable pod bought every three days forever after.
risks: 22 times earnings is modest, but free cash flow of $260M lags earnings because of manufacturing investment
Pump competition is intense and automated insulin delivery is becoming a commodity feature
opportunities: Revenue grew from $1.1B to $2.7B in four years and is $3.2B over the last twelve months
Analysts see about 30% upside, with 23 covering the stock
Type 2 diabetes is a far larger population than type 1 and Omnipod is now approved for it
watch: New patient starts, especially in type 2 diabetes.
